references.text: Moses recounts the event where he took the calf, burned it with fire, ground it to powder, and scattered the dust into the stream that flowed down from the mountain.
King Josiah burned the Asherah pole at the Kidron Brook and crushed it to powder, actions similar to those Moses performed with the golden calf.
Josiah smashed the altar in Bethel to powder and burned the Asherah pole, reflecting Moses' destruction of the golden calf.
King Asa broke his mother's Asherah image and burned it at the Kidron Brook, an act reminiscent of Moses' handling of the golden calf.
Josiah tore down the altars, smashed the Asherah images, and ground them to powder which he scattered on the graves, similar to Moses' destruction of the idol.
Isaiah describes the folly of idolatry and how man-made idols are worthless, underscoring the seriousness of Israel's sin with the golden calf.
Complementary parts of the same story showing the fall into sin and God's judgment on the idol.
